key_insight: ApexGO uses a generative AI pipeline to redesign peptide antibiotics that more effectively kill drug‑resistant bacteria; top candidates were validated in vitro and in mouse infection models, matching or outperforming standard antibiotics.
problem_solved: Addresses the slow, costly process of discovering optimized peptide antibiotics capable of overcoming antimicrobial resistance by automating sequence design and prioritizing candidates for experimental testing.
method: Generative model to propose novel or redesigned peptide sequences guided by objective functions for antimicrobial activity and developability.
In silico filtering and prioritization of candidates (e.g., predicted potency, toxicity/developability) to select top designs.
Experimental validation pipeline: laboratory microbiology assays followed by in vivo mouse infection studies to confirm efficacy.
impact: Demonstrates a practical ML→wet‑lab loop where generative models accelerate biologic drug design and produce therapeutically relevant candidates, encouraging ML practitioners to integrate predictive design and experimental validation in drug discovery workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: ApexGO model → candidate generation → in silico filtering → lab assays → mouse models (icons for each step).
Bar chart or heatmap comparing antimicrobial activity (e.g., kill rates or MICs) of ApexGO peptides vs. standard antibiotics across resistant strains.
Sequence-level visualization (sequence logo or alignment) highlighting common motifs/changes introduced by the model correlated with improved activity.
Outcome snapshot: schematic mouse infection before/after treatment or survival curve comparing ApexGO peptide vs control antibiotic.
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
